content.text: I have what I need: Article 11 contains a mutual indemnity, and Section 7.4 confirms third-party patent infringement claims against AbbVie fall within Harpoon's Section 11.2 indemnity.

input.quote: 11.2 Indemnification of AbbVie. Harpoon shall indemnify AbbVie, its Affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, and agents (the "AbbVie Indemnitees"), and defend and save each of them harmless, from and against any and all Losses in connection with any and all Third Party Claims incurred by or rendered against the AbbVie Indemnitees arising from or occurring as a result of: [***]
input.rationale: A counterparty (Harpoon) indemnity in our favour exists and is not one-way: Section 11.2 requires Harpoon to defend, indemnify and hold harmless the AbbVie Indemnitees (including Affiliates and their personnel) against Third Party Claims, and Sections 11.3-11.5 supply the standard procedure the playbook expects (prompt notice with no forfeiture for delay, indemnitor's option to assume defence, right to participate, settlement consent, cooperation, and expense reimbursement). Third-party IP infringement is within scope: Section 7.4 (Infringement Claims by Third Parties) expressly makes AbbVie's defence right "Subject to Section 11.2" and refers to "a claim that may be subject to Section 11.2" and to "Harpoon['s]... liab[ility] to indemnify any AbbVie Indemnitee", confirming that patent infringement claims arising from the Licensed Compound/Licensed Product are covered by Harpoon's indemnity. AbbVie's reciprocal indemnity in Section 11.1 is a standard mutual construct rather than a one-way indemnity for the counterparty's own activities. Notes (not deviations): the specific indemnity triggers in both 11.1 and 11.2 are redacted ([***]), so the precise breadth of Harpoon's IP/misconduct coverage and the narrowness of our reciprocal indemnity should be confirmed against the unredacted execution copy; there is also no indemnity super-cap, which favours us. On its readable material terms the clause meets the preferred position, so no redline is warranted.
